newsitem.title: ITALY: UN agency launches $19 million Sierra Leone aid.
newsitem.headline: UN agency launches $19 million Sierra Leone aid.

text.p: The U.N.'s World Food Programme said on Wednesday that it was launching a $19.4 million food aid operation for Sierra Leone to encourage the resettlement of thousands of people displaced in six years of civil war.
The Rome-based agency said in a statement some 775,000 people would benefit from the six-month emergency operation.

It said the majority of the aid would be given to support a resettlement, repatriation and rehabilitation programme and the remainder used to support Sierra Leonean refugees in Guinea and Liberian refugees in Sierra Leone who cannot yet return home.
"WFP field reports indicate more than one third of the country's four-million strong peopulation were displaced by the six-year civil war," the statement said.
The U.N. agency has been feeding more than half a million people since war first broke out in the early 1990s.

The government and rebels signed a peace deal on November 30 in Ivory Coast to end a war that killed at least 10,000 people, according to official estimates. But Sierra Leone rebels have said recently that government forces have violated the accord.
